summary: Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.
Kazutoshi Soma, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).
Kazutoshi Ueda was a linguist and Japanologist who studied under Karl Florenz and Georg von der Gabelentz. He succeeded Florenz and founded the Linguistic Society of Japan.

Kazuyoshi Hotta, a specialist in Indology and Buddhist studies, pursued doctoral studies and served as an administrator at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007). He later worked as a term-limited assistant professor at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai, served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989), and was vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and the University of Chicago (PhD under Mircea Eliade), and taught at Brown (~1961–1964) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~1969–1994).

Kehan Ding works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. Educated at Capital University of Economics and Business and the University of Edinburgh (PhD 2018–2024), Ding interned at Harvard (2021) and held teaching roles at Edinburgh (2019–2022, 2025).

Indologist and philosopher Kei Kataoka studied at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University. He held positions at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University, where he became a professor.
Kei Okusa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at Otani University, where he also holds a faculty appointment (attested 2026).

Keiichi Miyamoto is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, worked at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and served as lecturer, associate professor, and professor at Kokugakuin University from 1986.
Keiji Iwata, a religious studies scholar, studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1975–1980) and Otani University (~1986–1998).
Keiji Kokubu was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, Ritsumeikan University, and Nanzan University.

Keiji Nishitani was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Freiburg under Kitaro Nishida, Hajime Tanabe, and Martin Heidegger. He lectured at Otani University and served as professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964), succeeding Nishida.

Keiki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at and was affiliated with Kyoto University. He held a post as a JSPS fellow (attested 2020) and became a guest researcher at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Keiki Yabuki was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and Tokyo universities, he taught at Tendai Sect University, Shukyo University, the University of Tokyo, and as professor at Taisho University (~1926–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who has served as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and researcher at Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).
Keinin Hayashi, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, served as a former lecturer at Waseda University and full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Keir Strickland is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Bradford, the Highlands and Islands, and Durham under Robin Coningham, he taught at the University of the Highlands and Islands and La Trobe University.

Keishin Okamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Koyasan University (1959–1973; 2005–2009) and served as professor at Kochi University (~1970–1995).
